Bug_Title: "String.indexOf" should be used with correct ranges
Bug_Details:
Java 21 adds new String.indexOf methods that accept ranges ( beginIndex , to endIndex ) rather than just a
start index. A StringIndexOutOfBounds can be thrown when indicating an invalid range, namely when:
beginIndex > endIndex (eg: beginIndex and endIndex arguments are mistakenly reversed) beginIndex < 0 (eg: because the older String.indexOf(what, fromIndex) accepts negative values)
beginIndex > endIndex (eg: beginIndex and endIndex arguments are mistakenly reversed)
beginIndex < 0 (eg: because the older String.indexOf(what, fromIndex) accepts negative values)
Bug_Explanation: The code demonstrates two incorrect usages of the new String.indexOf method with beginIndex and endIndex parameters. In the first case, the beginIndex is greater than the endIndex, which is not a valid range, causing a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. In the second case, the beginIndex is negative, which is not allowed by the new method signature and also results in an exception.
Trigger_Explanation: The JUnit test cases trigger the bug by calling the showBug method with incorrect beginIndex and endIndex values, resulting in a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. The first test case uses a reversed range (beginIndex > endIndex), and the second test case uses a negative beginIndex, both of which are invalid and cause the exception to be thrown.
Test_Run_Result: Runninng test will fail system because of infinite loop.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate an infinite loop rather than a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException, suggesting the test did not confirm the triggering of the described bug.
